figure: M5 · 10 threads · mean over input seeds
subtitle: 128-bit security. Prove includes the witness commitment.
notes: Full Falcon is John's falcon_hybrid prover. Besides the ring and norm it proves SHAKE256 HashToPoint, and its statement is the public keys, messages and signatures, so Aerie has no counterpart here.

Each bar is the mean over input seeds of the median prove for that seed, and the line spans the lowest and highest seed. Two configurations have five seeds because one run each was disturbed by another session. With fixed inputs every prove replays one transcript, so each large grinding site is a single draw. With the small prime at 2^16 rows, the binder's grinding (its 28-bit linear site and 26 rounds) took 60M to 966M hashes depending on the seed, against about 275M expected.

The tight numerator (BITZ_FALCON_LINEAR_NUMERATOR=tight) counts the linear block's grinding numerator as m + d + 6 instead of m + d + B + 5. The block draws one multilinear point over rows and signatures, η and one merge coefficient, so the batch size B should not enter. It stays an accounting experiment until John confirms this.

The optimized binder replay is on by default only on Linux x86-64, so on the M5 it needs BITZ_BENCH_BINDER_REPLAY=on. Per-site grinding, the bridge rows and the small prime use the same switches as the algebraic prover.

On one thread (one seed) the hybrid proves in 2.35 s as built, 1.66 s with per-site grinding and 1.72 s with 2^16 rows, and verifies in 40 ms. Peak memory at 10 threads is 2.4 to 2.5 GiB in every configuration.
